chats.answer:
For a 100Ah LiFePO4 battery, my top picks are LiTime, Battle Born, Epoch, and Renogy, depending on your budget and intended use.

I'm assuming you want a 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 battery for an RV, solar system, camping setup, or backup power.

A typical 12.8V 100Ah battery stores 1,280Wh (1.28kWh) of energy. The biggest differences between brands are battery management system (BMS) quality, low-temperature protection, warranty, and price.

BatteryTrail

My recommendation

For most people, I'd choose the LiTime 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth. It offers a useful combination of capacity, monitoring, protection, and price without paying the premium for Battle Born.

Before buying, make sure the battery has a suitable low-temperature charge cutoff, fits your battery compartment, and supports your inverter's continuous current demand. A 100A BMS generally limits a 12V battery to roughly 1,280W nominal DC output.
